title: A valid PowerShell pipe such as `gh api x | jq .` is refused, and the refusal names no way out
why: Coordinator report 13:22 CST Nov 16 (relay; triage read no refusal text and no guard): a PowerShell command of the form `gh api x | jq .` is valid PowerShell and the guards refuse it. Triage searched steps for jq and powershell on 13:27 CST: pwsh-c-text-mode (done), pwsh-followups (doing), encoded-retry-after-refusal (ready) and refusal-names-way-out (doing) are near, none names this pipe. Not measured: which guard refuses it, how often, and in which shell. Mistake it risks: an agent re-sends the pipe in another form, which encoded-retry-after-refusal also refuses. Guard that would stop the harm: a test that runs this exact pipe through the Bash guards and shows it allowed, or a refusal that names the allowed form (refusal-names-way-out).
note: Ready.
